title_target: Describiendo un lugar en el pasado
learning_objectives: Can describe a place in the past using there was / there were.
scenario: María visita a su amiga Laura en su nuevo apartamento. Mientras toman un café, María le cuenta cómo era la casa de su infancia: un edificio viejo con un balcón grande, un ático lleno de muebles viejos y un sótano oscuro. Laura se sorprende y le hace preguntas sobre ese lugar del pasado.
introduction_md:
## Describiendo un lugar en el pasado

En esta lección vas a aprender a describir cómo era un lugar en el pasado. Esto es muy útil cuando quieres hablar de tu antigua casa, de un viaje o de un lugar que ya no existe.

**Vas a aprender:**

- **There was / There were** (había) para hablar del pasado.
- Vocabulario de la casa: *apartment*, *furniture*, *building*, *balcony*, *attic*, *basement*.

**¿Por qué es importante?**

Imagina que quieres contarle a un amigo cómo era la casa de tu abuela. Con esta lección podrás decir: *There was a big balcony* (Había un balcón grande).

¡Vamos a practicar con ejemplos de la vida real!
intro_target:
## Describing a place in the past

In this lesson, you will learn to describe how a place was in the past. This is very useful when you want to talk about your old house, a trip, or a place that no longer exists.

**You will learn:**

- **There was / There were** (there was / there were) to talk about the past.
- House vocabulary: *apartment*, *furniture*, *building*, *balcony*, *attic*, *basement*.

**Why is it important?**

Imagine you want to tell a friend how your grandmother's house was. With this lesson, you can say: *There was a big balcony*. 

Let's practice with real-life examples!

grammar_explanations.description_md_form:
Para describir un lugar en el pasado, usamos **there was** (singular) y **there were** (plural). Ambos significan *había* en español.

- **There was** + sustantivo singular: `There was a balcony.` (Había un balcón.)
- **There were** + sustantivo plural: `There were two buildings.` (Había dos edificios.)

La forma negativa es **there wasn't** (was not) y **there weren't** (were not): `There wasn't any furniture.` (No había muebles.)

Para preguntar, invertimos el orden: `Was there a basement?` (¿Había un sótano?) y `Were there any boxes?` (¿Había cajas?).

**Importante:** *there* no significa *allí* aquí; es parte de la estructura para decir que algo existe o existía.
grammar_explanations.description_md_target:
To describe a place in the past, we use **there was** (singular) and **there were** (plural). Both mean *there existed*.

- **There was** + singular noun: `There was a balcony.`
- **There were** + plural noun: `There were two buildings.`

The negative forms are **there wasn't** (was not) and **there weren't** (were not): `There wasn't any furniture.`

For questions, we invert the order: `Was there a basement?` and `Were there any boxes?`

**Note:** *there* does not mean *allí* here; it is part of the structure to say something existed.

callouts.text_md: **Recuerda:** *there was* para UNA cosa, *there were* para VARIAS cosas. Si dudas, mira el sustantivo: singular → was, plural → were.
**Error común:** No digas *there was two buildings*. Como *two buildings* es plural, necesitas **there were**.
**Cuidado:** *there* en esta estructura NO significa *allí*. *There was a balcony* = *Había un balcón*, no *Allí era un balcón*.

common_errors_es: Usar *there was* con sustantivos plurales: ✗ There was two buildings. → ✓ There were two buildings.
Olvidar la forma negativa contraída: ✗ There was not any furniture (correcto pero poco natural). → ✓ There wasn't any furniture.
Confundir *there* con *allí*: ✗ Allí was a balcony. → ✓ There was a balcony.
En preguntas, mantener el orden afirmativo: ✗ There was a basement? → ✓ Was there a basement?

notes_md_form:
## There was / There were: el pasado de "hay"

Para hablar de un lugar en el pasado, usamos **there was** (singular) y **there were** (plural). Es el pasado de *there is / there are*.

- **There was** a big balcony in my apartment. (Había un balcón grande en mi departamento.)
- **There were** two beds in the room. (Había dos camas en la habitación.)

**Ojo con el error clásico:** en español decimos "habían" para plural, pero en inglés **nunca** digas *there were* con *was*: *there were* es solo para plural. Tampoco uses *there was* con plural: ✗ *There was two beds.* → ✓ **There were** two beds.

## Trucos para recordar

- **Was** = singular (one thing): *There was an attic.*
- **Were** = plural (two or more): *There were three buildings.*
- Para negar: **there wasn't** / **there weren't**. Para preguntar: **Was there...?** / **Were there...?**

Piensa en tu casa o tu barrio: *There was a small basement. There were many trees.* ¡Así lo usas en tu vida real!
